Power Platform governance refers to the set of policies, practices, and tools used to manage and control the use of Power Platform within your organization. It aims to ensure that the platform is used efficiently, securely, and in compliance with organizationa
In this section, we explore some best practices to follow when establishing and implementing a governance strategy for Power Platform.
- Designate a Power Platform admin. Assign a dedicated administrative role to oversee operations, ensure compliance, and optimize performance.
- Support management at scale. Implement governance practices that support the efficient and secure management of Power Platform environments at scale, ensuring consistency and control across the organization.
- Establish an environment strategy. Develop a comprehensive strategy for creating, managing, and decommissioning environments to support organizational goals.
- Implement reactive governance controls. Manage and address actions and issues as they arise.
- Use agentic governance with Power Platform Admin in Cowork. Ask tenant governance questions, explore findings, and turn answers into reports and recurring briefings.
- Manage Dataverse for Teams environments. Develop strategies for managing Dataverse for Teams environments.

## Prevent oversharing
Power Platform is designed to be a low-code platform that enables users to create apps and flows quickly. However, this ease of use can lead to oversharing of apps and flows, which can pose security risks.
### Configure sharing limits
To enhance security and prevent oversharing within the Power Platform's default environment, limit how broadly users can share canvas apps, flows, and agents. Consider configuring sharing limits to maintain tighter control over access. Such limits reduce the risk of unauthorized usage, oversharing, and overuse without necessary 
### Limit sharing with everyone
If the default environment is a managed environment, prevent agents, apps, and flows from calling any service:
- Scope: Default environment only.
- Business: Empty.
- Non-Business: Empty.
- Blocked: All connectors. Blocking all connectors is available via advanced connector policies (ACP). Learn more in Advanced connector policies – Known limitations.
If you can't enable managed environments for the default environment, follow the other recommendations in this section: block new connectors, limit makers to prebuilt connectors, and limit custom connectors.

## Secure integration with Exchange
The Office 365 Outlook connector is one of the standard connectors that can't be blocked. It allows makers to send, delete, and reply to email messages in the mailboxes they have access to. When an app or flow sends an email using the Office 365 Outlook connector, it inserts specific SMTP headers in the message. You can use reserved phrases in the headers to identify whether an email originated from a flow or app.

Prereq: Yes, via /copilot/plan/microsoft-copilot-requirements. Deps: data foundation (SAM) before licence assignment; mailbox-grounded features need an Exchange Online mailbox; some features need OneDrive provisioned. FM: how-to; copilot-pr.
- **Copilot data protection architecture**, /copilot/plan/architecture-data-protection-auditing. Order: No (states it gives no deployment steps). Prereq: No. Deps: Copilot reads encrypted items only when the user holds VIEW and EXTRACT rights; SharePoint discovery settings shape grounding; Copilot audit/retention depend on Purview policies. FM: overview; copilot-pr.
- **Apply Zero Trust principles to Microsoft Copilot**, URL unchanged. Order: Yes, 7 steps: data protection and compliance, identity/access, app protection, device management, threat protection, Teams secure collaboration, least-privilege permissions (E3 then E5 in each). Prereq: Yes; each step deployed before assigning Copilot licences (waves in parallel). Deps: quick oversharing controls (Restricted SharePoint Search, DAG reports, Restricted Content Discovery) first, then labels, then revisit; device enrolment and compliance policies before requiring compliant devices. FM: concept-article; security-pr.
- **Manage your Copilot Studio projects**, /microsoft-copilot-studio/guidance/sec-gov-intro (+ sec-gov-phase1…3). Order: Yes: requirements, zoned governance, secure projects, testing, ALM, monitoring, model lifecycle, credit governance, checklist. Prereq: No. Deps: agents live in Power Platform environments, so zoning relies on environment groups, managed environments and data policies; licences and roles via Entra groups. FM: concept-article; businessapps-copilot-docs-pr. (/microsoft-copilot-studio/security-and-governance is an unordered concept-article.)

## 2. Secure collaboration and guests
- **Set up secure file sharing and collaboration with Teams** (archived). Order: loose: baseline tier first, then sensitive/highly sensitive, then external sharing. Prereq: No. Deps: tiers rely on sensitivity labels and Defender for Office 365. FM: solution-overview; officearchive-pr.
- **Collaborate with guests in a team (IT Admins)** (archived; old Teams checklist target). Order: Yes: Entra external collaboration, Teams guest access, M365 Groups guest settings, SharePoint org sharing, default links, create team, site sharing, invite. Prereq: implicit. Deps: Entra B2B settings override all lower layers; Teams guests need Groups guest settings on and SharePoint org sharing allowing guests; site sharing cannot exceed org level. FM: how-to; officearchive-pr. **...in a site**: same minus Teams step.
- **Microsoft 365 guest sharing settings reference** (archived). Order: No (by layer, Entra to site). Deps: Teams guest switch must be On before other guest settings apply; site domain lists cannot override org/Entra restrictions. FM: reference; officearchive-pr.
- **Recommended policies for specific Microsoft 365 workloads**, /security/zero-trust/zero-trust-identity-device-access-policies-workloads (Teams anchor). Order: No. Prereq: Yes, common identity/device policies first. Deps: CA covers Teams guests (B2B) but not external-access users; SharePoint unmanaged-device control auto-creates an Entra CA policy (P1). FM: best-practice; security-pr.
- **Policies for allowing guest/external access**, URL unchanged. Order: No. Prereq: Yes, builds on common policies. Deps: new MFA-always guest policy; exclude guests from risk-based MFA and device-compliance policies. FM: best-practice; security-pr.
- Extra: **Plan a Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration deployment**, /entra/architecture/secure-external-access-resources: ordered 8-article series ending with Teams/SharePoint/OneDrive external access and local-guest conversion. FM: concept-article; entra-docs-pr.

## 3. Teams
- **Guest access in Microsoft Teams**, /microsoftteams/guest-access. Order: No. Prereq: Yes; requires Entra, Groups and SharePoint settings, links to the archived checklist. FM: how-to; OfficeDocs-SkypeForBusiness-pr. No live checklist exists.
- **Manage external meetings and chat**, /microsoftteams/trusted-organizations-external-meetings-chat (`manage-external-access` redirects). Order: partial (org settings, then user policies). Prereq: Yes (Defender-managed blocked domains need MDO P1/P2 and a compatible external-access mode). Deps: org setting and user policy must both allow; the partner tenant must reciprocate. FM: article; same repo.
- **Security guide for Teams**, /microsoftteams/teams-security-guide. Order/Prereq: No. FM: reference. No ordered Teams "plan for security" page found.
- Archived **collaborate-teams-direct-connect** (shared channels): Prereq + order: enable shared channels in Teams, then Entra cross-tenant inbound/outbound B2B direct connect.

## 4. Global Secure Access (all FM repo entra-docs-pr)
- **GSA deployment guide intro**, /entra/architecture/gsa-deployment-guide-intro. Order: Yes: PoC sequence (prereqs, initial config, remote network, Microsoft traffic, Internet Access, Private Access), then initiate, plan, execute (pilot under 20 users, waves), monitor, close. Prereq: Yes. Deps: device registration before client; compliant-network CA needs a breakglass script to flip to report-only. FM: concept-article.
- **Internet Access guide**, /entra/architecture/gsa-deployment-guide-internet-access. Order: Yes: prereqs, pilot group, IA + Microsoft profiles, client, remote networks, web filtering, security profiles, CA linking, test. Deps: non-Baseline security profiles apply only via CA. FM: how-to.
- **Private Access guide**, /entra/architecture/gsa-deployment-guide-private-access. Order: Yes: profile, connectors, apps or Quick Access, client, CA, migrate segments, disable Quick Access. FM: how-to.
- **Compliant network check**, /entra/global-secure-access/how-to-compliant-network. Order: Yes: enable GSA CA signaling, create CA policy, test. Prereq: Yes. Deps: needs client or remote network; disabling signaling later can block users. FM: how-to.
- **Universal Tenant Restrictions**, /entra/global-secure-access/how-to-universal-tenant-restrictions. Order: Yes. Prereq: Yes: Microsoft traffic profile with Entra FQDNs tunnelled, clients or remote network, TRv2 default and partner policies first. FM: how-to.
- Client: /entra/global-secure-access/how-to-install-windows-client needs Entra joined/hybrid/registered device.

## 5. Power Platform (repo power-platform-pr)
- **Secure the default environment**, /power-platform/guidance/adoption/secure-default-environment. Order: Yes (sequenced sections, unnumbered): admin roles, communicate, managed environments, sharing limits, data policy, Exchange rules, tenant isolation. Prereq: No. Deps: sharing limits and block-all-connectors policy need managed environments; Outlook connector cannot be blocked, so Exchange mail-flow rules on Power Automate headers stop outbound mail; tenant isolation is separate from Entra tenant restrictions. FM: how-to.
- **Governance overview and strategy**, /power-platform/guidance/adoption/admin-best-practices: 7 practices, unnumbered. FM: concept-article.
- **Managed environments overview** (concept-article): licence entitlement; unmanaged developer environments must be managed by 2026-12-15. **Data policies** /power-platform/admin/wp-data-loss-prevention (overview) and **tenant isolation** /power-platform/admin/cross-tenant-restrictions (how-to): unordered; isolation affects Entra-auth connectors only.
- No single ordered Power Platform security baseline or deployment guide found.
EOF

  - Order: partial: org settings first, then user policies.
  - Prereq: Yes; blocked domains managed from Defender need MDO P1/P2.
  - Deps: the org setting and the user policy must both allow it, and the partner tenant must allow you back.
  - FM: article.
- **Teams security guide**, /microsoftteams/teams-security-guide. Not ordered, no prerequisites. FM: reference. I found no ordered "plan for security" page.
- Archived **collaborate-teams-direct-connect** (shared channels): enable shared channels in Teams first, then Entra cross-tenant B2B direct connect.

## 4. Global Secure Access (repo entra-docs-pr)
- **GSA deployment guide intro**, /entra/architecture/gsa-deployment-guide-intro.
  - Order: Yes. A PoC runs prereqs, config, remote network, Microsoft traffic, Internet Access, Private Access. The project then goes initiate, plan, execute (pilot, waves), monitor, close.
  - Prereq: Yes.
  - Deps: devices must be registered before the client; the client needs an Entra joined, hybrid joined or registered device. Compliant-network Conditional Access needs a breakglass plan.
  - FM: concept-article.
- **Internet Access guide**, /entra/architecture/gsa-deployment-guide-internet-access.
  - Order: Yes: prereqs, pilot group, Internet Access and Microsoft profiles, client, remote networks, web filtering, security profiles, Conditional Access linking, test.
  - Prereq: Yes.
  - Deps: security profiles other than Baseline apply only through Conditional Access.
  - FM: how-to.
- **Private Access guide**, /entra/architecture/gsa-deployment-guide-private-access.
  - Order: Yes: profile, connectors, apps or Quick Access, client, Conditional Access, migrate segments, disable Quick Access.
  - Prereq: Yes.
  - FM: how-to.
- **Compliant network check**, /entra/global-secure-access/how-to-compliant-network.
  - Order: Yes: enable GSA signaling for Conditional Access, create the policy, test.
  - Prereq: Yes.
  - Deps: needs the client or a remote network. Turning signaling off later can block users.
  - FM: how-to.
- **Universal Tenant Restrictions**, /entra/global-secure-access/how-to-universal-tenant-restrictions.
  - Order: Yes.
  - Prereq: Yes: a Microsoft traffic profile with the Entra FQDNs tunnelled, clients or a remote network, and the TRv2 default and partner policies first.
  - FM: how-to.

## 5. Power Platform (repo power-platform-pr)
- **Secure the default environment**, /power-platform/guidance/adoption/secure-default-environment.
  - Order: Yes, in sequenced but unnumbered sections: admin roles, communicate, managed environments, sharing limits, data policy, Exchange rules, tenant isolation.
  - Prereq: No.
  - Deps: sharing limits and the block-all-connectors policy need managed environments. The Outlook connector cannot be blocked, so Exchange mail-flow rules on Power Automate headers are what stop outbound mail.
  - FM: how-to.
- **Governance overview and strategy**, /power-platform/guidance/adoption/admin-best-practices. Seven unnumbered practices. FM: concept-article.
- **Managed environments overview** (concept-article): it is a licence entitlement, and unmanaged developer environments must be made managed by 2026-12-15.
- **Data policies**, /power-platform/admin/wp-data-loss-prevention (overview), and **tenant isolation**, /power-platform/admin/cross-tenant-restrictions (how-to): neither is ordered. Tenant isolation affects only connectors that use Entra authentication, and it is separate from Entra tenant restrictions.
- I found no single ordered Power Platform security baseline or deployment guide.
